title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
gist: An InfoQ webinar panel (ThoughtWorks, privacy and financial-AI practitioners) argues production agentic AI fails silently through semantic and embedding drift, that human code review cannot scale with coding agents, and that agents need non-human identities, tiered access and living evals; deployment approval stays a business decision.

insights.claim: AI systems fail differently from traditional software: they produce convincing inaccuracies rather than crashing, so standard health checks and tracing can stay green while output is wrong.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Reliability monitoring for AI products must measure output correctness, not just uptime; watch vendors selling AI observability.
insights.quote: AI fails differently from traditional software by generating convincing inaccuracies rather than crashing

insights.claim: Text-to-SQL agents often flatten domain-specific concepts (e.g. treating 'member' identically across sales and customer support), causing subtle hidden errors in downstream business analytics that pass standard tracing.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Analytics built on LLM-generated SQL can carry undetected errors; semantic-layer and eval tooling is a needed control.

insights.claim: An unannounced background update to an embedding model shifted the vector distance distribution in a financial compliance agent that blocked prohibited investment advice via similarity thresholds, producing false positive and false negative spikes while all infrastructure health checks stayed green.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Silent upstream model updates are a vendor-dependency risk for regulated AI; pin versions and monitor distributions.

themes.theme: Scaling code review against coding agents

insights.claim: Coding agents generate production code faster than humans can review it, and line-by-line manual review cannot scale with high-velocity agent output.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Review capacity is the bottleneck of AI-assisted development; tools that automate verification gain relevance.
insights.quote: coding agents are generating production code faster than humans can review

insights.claim: Teams should automate tactical style and syntax checks in CI/CD and reserve human oversight for high-level architecture, business intent and non-functional requirements, and shift left to evaluate intent at the harness level before pull requests are generated.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Signals demand for harness/CI automation and intent-level evaluation tooling.

insights.claim: Mutation testing is resurging as a way to verify that automated test suites truly evaluate logic rather than merely satisfy code-coverage metrics.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Coverage metrics are weak proof of quality for AI-written code; mutation testing is a growing practice.

insights.claim: Evals should be treated as permanent, living infrastructure rather than static pre-release checklists, using continuous online span-level tracing to feed production edge cases back into offline benchmark suites.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Continuous eval and tracing is an ongoing spend category for AI teams, not a one-off launch cost.
insights.quote: evals must be treated as permanent, living infrastructure rather than static pre-release checklists

insights.claim: RAG pipelines can inadvertently retrieve sensitive documents, and models memorize training data, which can be used to de-anonymize information or expose API keys.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: New leak surfaces (prompts, context windows, retrieved documents) widen the data-privacy attack surface for enterprise AI.

insights.claim: Prompt engineering should not be relied on for system defence; Jarmul advocates systematic red teaming, continuous threat modeling, strict functional scopes for autonomous agents and scaled-up observability.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Guardrails enforced outside the model are the credible security layer; favours security tooling vendors.
insights.quote: Jarmul cautioned against relying on prompt engineering for system defence
insights.locator: To address privacy and security risks

insights.claim: To limit the blast radius of autonomous agents, treat each agent like a new engineering hire: distinct non-human identities, tiered access separating read-only from reversible write actions, versioned third-party MCP dependencies, and API secrets isolated outside the agent runtime.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Agent identity and access management is an emerging product category.
insights.quote: treating every AI agent like a new engineering hire

insights.claim: A malicious repository configuration (the GitSpawn vulnerability) can execute unauthorized code during routine commands.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Developer-tooling supply-chain risk grows as agents run routine commands automatically.
insights.locator: Chandrasekaran also referenced the GitSpawn vulnerability

insights.claim: While engineering, security and privacy teams validate guardrails, deployment approval of agentic systems remains a strategic business decision.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Adoption pace is gated by business risk owners, not only engineers.
insights.quote: deployment approval remains a strategic business decision
